themes_detail.label: Street Signs Vanishing
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 256% increase (z-score: 3.68)—suggesting coordinated theft, vandalism, or rapid deterioration across Lower Manhattan that poses navigation and safety hazards.
evidence: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (256% spike, z-score: 3.68)
Sustained baseline of only ~1.1 complaints/week suggests sudden acceleration is anomalous
Community board has repeatedly requested 'Repair or provide new street lights' (infrastructure underfunding)
reporting_angles: Are street signs being stolen or systematically removed? Canvass affected blocks.
Is DOT experiencing a maintenance backlog that has suddenly become visible?

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicles Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints exploded 2 weeks ago to 3 complaints versus a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69, highest severity ranking)—indicating a sudden influx of abandoned or disabled vehicles clogging Lower Manhattan streets.
evidence: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline over 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69—highest z-score in dataset)
Severity rated 'high' in automated analysis, indicating clustering or severity of reported incidents
Suggests either sudden enforcement wave, vehicle abandonment event, or street blockage pattern
reporting_angles: Did a specific triggering event (flood, contamination, construction) cause vehicles to be abandoned?
How is NYPD/DOT currently clearing these; what is the backlog?

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints surged LAST WEEK to 6 complaints versus a baseline of 1.8 per week—a 243% increase (z-score: 4.39)—signaling potential coordinated food safety failures or restaurant violations across the district that warrant DOH investigation.
evidence: 6 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (243% spike, z-score: 4.39)
Community board has requested 'Other programs to address public health issues' repeatedly—unmet infrastructure gap
Lower Manhattan has high density of restaurants and food vendors (Vendor Enforcement is top 311 complaint category at 1489 total)
reporting_angles: Which restaurants/vendors appear in multiple food poisoning complaints? Cross-reference with DOH violation history.
Is this related to the Outdoor Dining spike (500% increase 2 weeks ago)? Are temporary dining setups poorly regulated?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Acceleration
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints rose LAST WEEK to 9 versus a baseline of 3.9 per week—a 132% increase (z-score: 5.53)—suggesting organized waste disposal or construction debris dumping in Lower Manhattan streets and public spaces.
evidence: 9 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (132% spike, z-score: 5.53)
Community board has repeatedly requested 'Provide more on-street trash cans and recycling containers'—suggesting infrastructure inadequacy fuels overflow
Correlates with Street Condition complaints (612 total over 90 days, third-highest category)
reporting_angles: Are construction sites (1190 DOB permits filed in last 90 days) dumping debris illegally?
Map the dumping locations—is it concentrated near specific blocks or transit hubs?

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped LAST WEEK to 35 versus a baseline of 16.1 per week—a 117% increase (z-score: 4.01)—indicating a sudden escalation in outdoor commercial or construction noise disrupting pedestrians across Lower Manhattan.
evidence: 35 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 16.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (117% spike, z-score: 4.01)
Noise complaints collectively represent 862 complaints over 90 days (6% of all 311 volume), with street/sidewalk now surging
Correlates with Outdoor Dining spike (500% increase 2 weeks ago)—may reflect return of outdoor service noise
reporting_angles: Is the noise tied to outdoor dining expansion? Interview affected residents near open-air dining clusters.
Are construction sites (1190 permits) operating outside permitted hours?
